## Working directory (IMPORTANT)
Work ONLY from `/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.claude/worktrees/feature+sma-331-runtime-axum`. Branch `feature/sma-331-paigasus-helikon-runtime-axum-restssewebsocket-server`.
- NEVER run branch-moving/tree-resetting git (`checkout <branch>`, `switch`, `reset --hard`, `worktree`, `clean`). Shared tree. Only `git add <explicit paths>` + `git commit`. NEVER `git add -A`.
- Signed commits (1Password). On "failed to fill whole buffer", STOP + report BLOCKED, don't bypass signing.

Read each target file before editing. Keep every change minimal and focused. Doc every new public item (the crate has `missing_docs` under `-D warnings`).

## Fixes

### A. `src/server.rs` — router-wide auth gate (SECURITY, the most important fix)
Currently `AuthLayer` is only invoked inside `create_run`, so `GET /agents`, `GET /openapi.json`, and `GET /agents/{name}/runs/{id}/events` are NOT authenticated when `state.auth` is configured. Move auth to a router-level middleware so EVERY route is gated:
1. In `router()`, when `self.state.auth.is_some()`, wrap the router with an auth middleware via `axum::middleware::from_fn_with_state(self.state.clone(), auth_middleware::<Ctx>)`. Keep `router()` PURE (no spawn).
2. Implement `async fn auth_middleware<Ctx>(State(state): State<AppState<Ctx>>, req: axum::extract::Request, next: axum::middleware::Next) -> Result<Response, ServerError>`: if `state.auth` is `Some(auth)`, split `let (mut parts, body) = req.into_parts();`, call `auth.authenticate(&mut parts).await` — on `Err(rej)` return `Err(ServerError::Unauthorized(rej))`; on Ok, reassemble `Request::from_parts(parts, body)` (so any identity the AuthLayer inserted into `parts.extensions` flows downstream) and `Ok(next.run(req).await)`. If `state.auth` is None, just `next.run(req)`.
3. In `create_run` (handlers/runs.rs), REMOVE the per-handler `authenticate(...)` call (the layer now does it). The `ContextProvider::build(&parts, ...)` still reads any identity from `parts.extensions` exactly as before — do not change that.
Add a focused integration test (in `tests/server.rs` or a new `tests/auth.rs`) with a mock `AuthLayer` that rejects when an `Authorization` header is absent: assert that WITH auth configured, `GET /agents` returns 401 without the header and 200 with it. (Mock lives in the test file.)

### B. `src/handlers/runs.rs` — panic-safe terminal bookkeeping (STABILITY)
The spawned writer task can panic before `mark_terminal()` / `note_terminal()`, stranding subscribers forever. Add a drop-guard so terminal state is ALWAYS recorded:
- Define a small guard struct (e.g. `struct TerminalGuard { log: Arc<EventLog>, registry: Arc<RunRegistry>, run_id: Uuid }`) whose `Drop` calls `self.log.mark_terminal();` and `self.registry.note_terminal(self.run_id, Instant::now());`. Both are idempotent (`mark_terminal` just sets the flag; `note_terminal` only stamps if `terminal_at` is None), so running on both the normal path and a panic-unwind is safe.
- In the writer task, construct the guard at the top (holding clones of `handle.log`, the registry Arc, and `run_id`). Let the existing match arms keep doing their work (drain events into the log on Ok; set `start_error` on Err). You may REMOVE the now-redundant explicit `mark_terminal()`/`note_terminal()` calls at the end of the task (the guard covers them) OR keep them (idempotent) — prefer removing the explicit trailing ones and letting the guard own terminal bookkeeping, but keep the `start_error` set on the Err arm.
- Add a test (in `tests/concurrency.rs`) using a runner or agent whose stream PANICS partway (e.g. a test `Agent` whose `run` returns a stream that panics, or a `Runner` whose `run_streamed` future panics) and assert a one-shot request still returns (within a `tokio::time::timeout`) rather than hanging. If a panicking-stream test is too fiddly to make deterministic, at minimum keep the guard and note in your report that the panic path is covered by inspection.

### C. `src/handlers/runs.rs` — reject invalid/conflicting transport selectors (CONTRACT)
`?stream=foo` / `?mode=bar` currently fall back to one-shot, and `?mode=async&stream=sse` silently prefers async. Add `impl RunQuery { fn validate(&self) -> Result<(), ServerError> }` that: returns `ServerError::BadRequest` if `mode` is `Some(v)` and `v != "async"`; if `stream` is `Some(v)` and `v != "sse"`; and if both async and sse are requested together. Call `query.validate()?` at the top of `create_run`. Add a test asserting `?mode=bogus` → 400 and `?mode=async&stream=sse` → 400.

### D. `src/dto.rs` — tighten RunRequest (reject mixed/extra fields) (CONTRACT)
`RunRequestHelper` (untagged) accepts `{"input":"x","messages":[...]}` (drops the extra) and ignores unknown fields. Replace the untagged helper with a single `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)] struct RunRequestRaw { input: Option<String>, messages: Option<Vec<Item>> }`, and in `RunRequest`'s `Deserialize` (or `into_agent_input`/a `TryFrom`) validate that EXACTLY ONE of `input`/`messages` is `Some` — error (custom serde error or a ServerError at the call site, whichever the current structure uses) if both are set or neither is set or an unknown field is present. Keep the existing public `into_agent_input()` behavior for the valid cases. Update/extend tests: `{"input":"x"}` ok, `{"messages":[...]}` ok, `{"input":"x","messages":[...]}` rejected, `{"input":"x","extra":1}` rejected, `{}` rejected. (Note: `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` does NOT compose with `#[serde(untagged)]` — that's why the single-struct approach is required.)

### E. `src/error.rs` — clamp auth-rejection status (SECURITY)
In `ServerError`'s `IntoResponse`, the `Unauthorized(rej)` arm returns `rej.status` unchanged; a buggy `AuthLayer` could return 2xx/3xx. Clamp: if `rej.status` is `UNAUTHORIZED` or `FORBIDDEN`, use it; otherwise use `StatusCode::UNAUTHORIZED`. Add/extend the `status_mapping` test to assert: `Unauthorized` with a 401 → 401, with a 403 → 403, with a 200 → clamped to 401; and `Internal` → 500.

### F. `src/event_log.rs` — reject zero capacity (DEFENSIVE)
`EventLog::new(0)` would evict every event including the terminal. Add `assert!(max_events > 0, "max_events must be > 0");` at the top of `new` (mirrors `InMemorySessionProvider::new`). No new test required (a debug assert), but you may add a `#[should_panic]` test if quick.

### G. `src/handlers/events.rs` — break on `Message::Close(_)` (STABILITY)
In `handle_socket`'s `select!`, the `socket.recv()` arm currently treats all `Some(Ok(_))` frames the same (ignored). A graceful `Message::Close(_)` arrives as `Some(Ok(Message::Close(_)))` and is ignored, so the server keeps sending until a send error. Add an explicit match: on `Some(Ok(axum::extract::ws::Message::Close(_)))` → break; other `Some(Ok(_))` → ignore (continue); `None`/`Some(Err(_))` → break (as now).

### H. `src/registry.rs` — atomic terminal stamping + queue insertion (RACE)
`note_terminal` currently stamps `terminal_at` (releasing the lock) before taking a write lock to push into `completion_order`, allowing a concurrent `sweep` to interleave. Refactor so both happen under a SINGLE `inner.write()` critical section: take the write lock first, get the handle clone, lock `terminal_at`; if `None`, stamp it AND `inner.completion_order.push_back(id)` while still holding the write lock. (This is the lock order `inner` → `terminal_at`, matching `sweep`, so no deadlock.) Keep the existing registry tests passing.

### I. `src/server.rs` — validate `max_sessions(0)` (ROBUSTNESS)
The builder accepts `max_sessions(0)`, but `build()` → `InMemorySessionProvider::new(0)` asserts and PANICS. In `build()`, if no custom `session_provider` was set AND `self.max_sessions == 0`, return `Err(ServerError::BadRequest("max_sessions must be greater than 0"))` BEFORE constructing the provider. Add a test asserting `builder().max_sessions(0)...build()` is `Err`.

### J. `src/handlers/openapi.rs` — sync the OpenAPI stubs (DOC ACCURACY)
The `_create_run_doc` `#[utoipa::path]` stub is missing the `stream` and `mode` query params and the `400/401/403/500` responses; `_events_doc` is missing the `400` invalid-UUID response. Add them as utoipa `params(...)` and `responses(...)` entries with clear descriptions. NOTE: `RunResponse` is intentionally NOT a `ToSchema`, so document the `200` response with a DESCRIPTION only (no `body = RunResponse`) — do not force a ToSchema derive. Keep `_events_doc`'s `101` WebSocket response. Ensure `cargo test --features openapi --test openapi` still passes.

### K. Test hardening (avoid CI hangs / weak asserts)
- `tests/ws.rs`: wrap the `ws.next().await` collection loop in `ws_replays_completed_run_then_closes` with `tokio::time::timeout` (e.g. 5s) so a regression fails fast instead of hanging. AND in the 404 tests (`ws_unknown_id_404_before_upgrade` and the name-mismatch test), assert the handshake error is specifically a 404: match `tokio_tungstenite::connect_async(...)` `Err` as `tungstenite::Error::Http(resp)` and assert `resp.status() == 404` (instead of bare `is_err()`).
- `tests/concurrency.rs`: wrap the WS drain loop and the `tokio::join!`/concurrent waits in `tokio::time::timeout` so they fail fast on regression.
- `tests/server.rs`: in `duplicate_agent_name_is_build_error` and `build_without_context_provider_errors`, assert the specific error (match the `ServerError` variant and/or that the message contains "duplicate agent name" / the missing-context wording) instead of bare `is_err()`.

### L. `docs/book/src/reference/crates.md` — fix the stale facade version
The `paigasus-helikon` facade row shows `0.3.12`; this PR bumps it to `0.4.14`. Update that row's version to `0.4.14`. (Leave the `2026-06-30` "current as of" date AS-IS — it is correct for the author's local date.)

## Verify (run ALL and report each result)
- `cargo test -p paigasus-helikon-runtime-axum --all-features` — whole crate suite (unit + all integration files) green, including your new tests.
- `cargo fmt --all` then `cargo clippy -p paigasus-helikon-runtime-axum --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

- `mdbook build docs/book` clean.
If any fix fights the compiler in a way you cannot resolve after genuine effort, implement the others, and report the specific blocker (don't ship something broken or that weakens a test/assertion).

## Commit
- ONE commit: `fix(runtime-axum): SMA-331 address CodeRabbit review (auth gate, panic-safety, validation, test hardening)`. Stage explicit paths for every file you changed (list them). NEVER `git add -A`.

## Report

---
name: reference_coderabbit_graphql_control_chars
description: CodeRabbit review-comment bodies fetched via gh api graphql can contain unescaped control chars that break jq; fetch bodies via REST instead.
metadata:
  type: reference
---

When pulling CodeRabbit review threads in the coderabbit-loop, the `gh api graphql`
`reviewThreads { comments { body } }` response can contain **literal unescaped control
characters (U+0000–U+001F)** in the `body` field, which is invalid JSON and makes `jq`
fail with `Invalid string: control characters ... must be escaped`. This breaks both raw
interpolation and `jq -c` on the response.

**Fix:** fetch thread *metadata* (ids, path, line, author — no body) via GraphQL, then
fetch each comment's body via REST `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/comments/{commentId}`
(or `gh api .../issues/{pr}/comments`), which escapes control chars properly. Reply uses
the integer `databaseId` (REST `.../pulls/{pr}/comments/{commentId}/replies`); resolve uses
the GraphQL node `threadId` — see [[reference_coderabbit_status_check]].

Also: a `reviewThreads(first:1)` existence probe undercounts — use `first:100` to get the
real thread count. And CodeRabbit was unusually slow on a large PR (~30 min initial review,
~8 min incremental re-reviews); poll the `gh pr checks` CodeRabbit row (pending→pass) plus
the unresolved-thread count rather than guessing. "Outside diff range" findings still aren't
threads — handle via a top-level PR comment per [[reference_coderabbit_outside_diff_no_thread]].

input.title: runtime-axum follow-ups: SSE/WS start-error frame, --no-default-features CI gate, EventLog replay perf
input.description:
Deferred polish for `paigasus-helikon-runtime-axum`, surfaced during the SMA-331 final review + CodeRabbit pass on PR #129 (merged, published `0.1.0`). All non-blocking — the crate shipped with both acceptance criteria met and the full workspace gate green.

## 1. SSE/WebSocket synthetic error frame on the start-error path
When `Runner::run_streamed` returns an outer `Err(RunError)` (e.g. a session backend is unavailable), the writer records `start_error` + `mark_terminal()` with no event appended. One-shot correctly maps this to HTTP 500, but the SSE and WebSocket transports just close cleanly with no final error frame. Spec §6 says "streams emit a final synthetic error frame, then close." Currently unreachable with the default in-memory provider (which never fails to start), so low-impact, but a custom `SessionProvider`/`Runner` could hit it.

**Fix:** in the SSE/WS subscriber paths, when the run ended via `start_error` (terminal with no `RunCompleted`/`RunFailed`), emit a synthetic `run_failed`-style frame before closing.

## 2. `--no-default-features` build in CI
`runtime-axum`'s `openapi` feature gating is correct by inspection (and builds locally), but no standing CI gate compiles the crate with `--no-default-features`. A feature-gating regression would slip past the `--all-features`-only matrix.

**Fix:** add a `cargo build -p paigasus-helikon-runtime-axum --no-default-features` step (or matrix entry) to `ci.yml`.

## 3. `EventLog` replay perf for very large rings
`EventLog::subscribe` replays by repeated single-element `read_from` calls → O(n²) allocations/copies for N retained events. Bounded by the per-run cap (default 10k), so fine in practice, but a pathological large-run replay amplifies it (mild DoS-amplification angle). The backing `VecDeque::with_capacity(max_events.min(64))` also reallocs ~4× for production-sized logs.

**Fix:** batch-drain events into the subscriber's cursor state instead of one-at-a-time; size the initial capacity sensibly.

---
